items.mainDefect: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins who are not owners are denied.

secondary.defect: Any attendee matched by email can add guests, which is a looser permission than the organizer/admin model.

items.mainDefect: The blacklist and existing-attendee checks are case-sensitive, so mixed-case emails bypass the blacklist and duplicate existing attendees.

secondary.defect: Duplicate emails inside the submitted guest list are not removed on the server.

items.mainDefect: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so filtered-out or existing attendees get the wrong email.

secondary.defect: updateCalendarAttendees has no error handling and runs after the DB write, so a calendar failure leaves the attendees saved while the request returns an error.

items.mainDefect: The blacklist and attendee dedupe checks compare guest emails without lowercasing them, so changing the case bypasses both checks.

secondary.defect: The isAttendee permission check at line 52 compares attendee.email to user.email case-sensitively.

items.mainDefect: Duplicate emails within the submitted guests list are not deduplicated on the server, so createMany inserts duplicate attendees.

secondary.defect: The blacklist check is case-sensitive because the guest email is not lowercased.
sendAddGuestsEmails is passed guests instead of uniqueGuests.

items.mainDefect: The error toast string is always truthy, so the unable_to_add_guests fallback never runs and that translation key is dead.

secondary.defect: Users see a raw tRPC error code such as 'BAD_REQUEST:' in the toast.

items.mainDefect: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so it means admin AND owner instead of admin OR owner.

secondary.defect: The FORBIDDEN message key 'you_do_not_have_permission' is missing from en/common.json, so the toast may show the raw key.
